hero.title: About OSA Observatory
paragraphs: The African Sovereignty Observatory (OSA Observatory) is an independent scientific infrastructure dedicated to observing, measuring and analysing the sovereignty trajectories of African states.
OSA develops methods based exclusively on primary data that is auditable, reproducible, and independent of any subjective perception.

mission.title: Our Mission
paragraphs: Observe phenomena, measure trajectories, identify emerging risks, and analyse the mechanisms likely to durably influence the exercise of sovereignty.
OSA does not pass judgment on states. It objectively documents observable facts to inform research, public policy, and strategic decision-making.

why.title: Why Measure Sovereignty?
paragraphs: Sovereignty is not a fixed state. It evolves continuously under the effect of economic, human, digital, environmental, geopolitical, energy, monetary, institutional and security factors.
OSA measures trajectories rather than simple instantaneous positions, in order to better understand the dynamics of transformation of African states.

World governance indicators are built 60-70% on surveys of Western experts — they measure what observers think, not what states do. The corruption perception index relies 80% on private sector surveys. Two states with identical practices can score very differently depending on who is asked. OSA proposes a different approach: observing the real capabilities of African states from verifiable behavioural data.

programs.subtitle: Observe and measure
programs.body: The Index of African Sovereignty measures sovereignty trajectories through the L1 → L2 → L3 methodological pipeline.

programs.subtitle: Observe and identify
programs.body: Autonomous Observable Phenomena identify objectifiable, reproducible and measurable phenomena likely to affect the effective exercise of sovereignty. They produce no index, score or ranking, and do not constitute a judgment on public policy.

programs.subtitle: Observe and alert
programs.body: AMAR identifies situations requiring heightened vigilance, based on rupture signals, strategic analyses and business rules. It is not a trajectory measure: a high score signals a situation to monitor, not a judgment on the state concerned.

programs.subtitle: Observe and detect
programs.body: GENECO detects the economic mechanisms likely to durably affect the exercise of sovereignty in a conflict context.

approach.title: Our Scientific Approach
paragraphs: All data used by OSA comes from observable primary sources.
Processing is fully documented, historised, auditable and reproducible in order to guarantee scientific transparency.

governance.title: Scientific Governance
governance.body: The OSA Observatory operates under the oversight of a Scientific Committee responsible for validating methodological decisions, approving publication cycles, and ensuring doctrinal integrity. The first institutional publication is scheduled for September 2027. Data for 2020-2024 is available at OFFICIAL status. 2025 data is at PRELIMINARY status pending validation.

closing.title: A New Approach to Sovereignty
closing.body: OSA Observatory is a scientific platform for observing phenomena, measuring trajectories, identifying situations requiring heightened vigilance, and detecting mechanisms likely to durably affect the exercise of sovereignty.

methodology.title: OSA Scientific Methodology
methodology.intro: The OSA scientific pipeline computes the ISA from observed, primary, auditable data — never surveys, never expert estimates. It is also the common foundation for the POA, AMAR and GENECO programmes. The methodology follows the OSA P7E consequentialist doctrine.
methodology.doctrine_text: For decades, Africa has been evaluated through indices built on perceptions. OSA proposes a different approach: observing the real capabilities of African states from verifiable behavioural data, tracking their trajectories over time and informing public decisions with facts rather than perceptions.
methodology.normalisation_text: Min-max normalisation: score = (value - min) / (max - min) for positive indicators, inverted for negative ones. Bounds are frozen on the 2010-2020 reference period (v1_2026) — ensuring new data does not shift historical scores.
methodology.weighting_text: Equal weighting within each pillar — each active indicator receives 1/n weight where n is the number of indicators with observed data. The 10 pillars are equally weighted in the ISA composite. Weights are automatically renormalized when indicators are activated or deactivated.
rules: Every indicator is a primary observable datum — collected from an audited, geolocated, dated source
Perception-based indicators (WGI, CPI) are permanently excluded — demonstrated OECD evaluator bias
No country is compared to another — each is observed against its own sovereign trajectory
Indicators without observed data do not participate in weighting
methodology.architecture_intro: The L1 → L2 → L3 pipeline feeds the ISA. POAs draw on L1 and dedicated business-rule calculations, independently of the L2 and L3 layers.

isa.subtitle: Observe and measure
isa.body: The Index of African Sovereignty measures the sovereignty trajectories of African states through the full L1 → L2 → L3 pipeline.

poa.subtitle: Observe and identify
poa.body: Autonomous Observable Phenomena (POA) identify objectifiable, reproducible and measurable phenomena likely to affect the effective exercise of sovereignty. They draw on validated L1-level data together with dedicated business-rule calculations, independently of the L2 and L3 layers. They produce no index, ranking or weighting: they document observable phenomena that researchers and decision-makers can analyse.

methodology.strategic_text: The results produced by the ISA feed a strategic analysis engine that identifies strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, threats, trajectories, trends and confidence levels. This analysis relies exclusively on reproducible calculations performed from observed data.

amar.subtitle: Observe and alert
amar.body: AMAR draws on the results of the strategic analysis to identify situations requiring heightened vigilance. The engine combines ISA trajectories, strategic analyses, historical data and confidence levels with trigger business rules. It is not a trajectory measure: a high score signals a situation to monitor, not a judgment on the state concerned.

geneco.subtitle: Observe and detect
geneco.body: GENECO detects the economic mechanisms likely to durably affect the exercise of sovereignty in a conflict context. It combines ISA results, strategic analyses, specialised observations and dedicated business rules.

data.title: Open Data & API
data.opendata_text: ISA sovereign trajectories for 54 African states (2010-{year}) are freely available under the Creative Commons CC-BY-NC-4.0 licence. Attribution to the OSA Observatory is required. Commercial exploitation is prohibited without a written institutional agreement.
data.api_text: Interactive documentation for all OSA Observatory API endpoints. Researchers and affiliated institutions may test queries, explore data structures, and integrate sovereign indicators into their own analytical frameworks.
data.access_text: SUBSCRIBER and ADVANCED affiliates access feasibility studies, proof-of-concept documents, and sovereign intelligence reports. Six affiliation categories: State, Regional Organisation, International Organisation, Academic Institution, Private Sector, Development Bank.

participate.title: E-Participation
participate.intro: Contribute to the quality of African sovereign data. Report an anomaly, propose a primary source, or submit a methodological contribution to the Scientific Committee.

DATA_SIGNAL.label: Data signal
DATA_SIGNAL.desc: Report an anomaly, incorrect value, or suggest an alternative primary source for a specific indicator.

SOURCE_PROPOSAL.label: Source proposal
SOURCE_PROPOSAL.desc: Suggest a new primary data source that could improve coverage of a sovereign pillar.

METHODOLOGICAL.label: Methodological contribution
METHODOLOGICAL.desc: Propose a new indicator, a methodological improvement, or a doctrinal comment for Scientific Committee review.

participate.success_msg: Thank you. Your contribution has been transmitted to the OSA Scientific Committee.

pillar.doctrine_text: This pillar follows the OSA P7E consequentialist doctrine: only observed, verifiable data is used. Perception-based indicators are excluded. Equal weighting is applied across active indicators with available data.
